Let \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(\ell=h/k^{1/d}\), and \(\delta=h^\gamma=\ell^S\). The published second-order localized \(U\)-statistic/R-learner suggests the upper inequality
\[
h^\gamma+\ell^S+
\sqrt{\frac1{nh^d}\left(1+\frac{k}{nh^d}\right)}.
\]
In the nuisance-dominated region, balancing these terms gives
\[
D=1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{2S},\qquad
h=n^{-1/(\gamma D)},\qquad
k=n^{(d/S-d/\gamma)/D},\qquad
\delta=n^{-1/D}.
\]
For \(S\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), take \(h=n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)}\) and \(k\asymp nh^d\). At equality the two prescriptions agree and every displayed term is \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\); no dyadic summation or divergent integral occurs, hence no logarithm would arise. This is an upper-bound blueprint, not a completed same-class theorem: KBRW’s theorem has additional Gram/pilot regularity and an interior-point setup that still must be checked for the one-sided uniform-cube estimator. [KBRW, Theorem 2 and equation (14)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11960818/)

The lower-bound obstruction is structural. Robins’ mixture factorization requires partition-local dependence. Disjoint cell bumps satisfy that condition, but exact average cancellation forces the contrast compensation to vary on scale \(\ell\), whose \(\gamma\)-Hölder norm is
\[
\asymp \delta\ell^{-\gamma}=\ell^{S-\gamma}\to\infty
\]
when \(S<\gamma\). Overlapping bumps can make \(\sum_jB_j^2\) a broad \(\gamma\)-smooth profile, but then observations depend on several common signs and the partition-local hypothesis fails. Retaining uniform mass on the perforated construction’s transition regions instead leaves a mixture mismatch of size \(\delta\) on volume \(h^d\), producing the product contribution
\[
nh^d\delta^2=n\delta^{\,2+d/\gamma}.
\]
For \(S<d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), \(D>2+d/\gamma\), so this quantity diverges at \(\delta=n^{-1/D}\). Thus neither filling the holes nor invoking the Robins theorem controls the required product mixtures. [Robins–Tchetgen–Li–van der Vaart, Theorem 2.1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5884174/)
